title: Understanding One-Hot Encoding
text: One-hot encoding transforms categorical variables into a set of binary variables. Each category becomes a column, and a row has a $$1$$ in the column corresponding to its category and 0s elsewhere.

title: Columns After One-Hot Encoding
text: The 'sex' column has two categories: 'male' and 'female'. The $$'embark_{town'}$$ column has five categories: 'Southampton', 'Cherbourg', 'Queenstown', 'London', 'Oxford'.

title: Calculating Total Columns
text: After one-hot encoding, the 'sex' column will have $$1$$ column (since one category can be inferred), and the $$'embark_{town'}$$ column will have $$4$$ columns (since one category can be inferred).
